title: The Launch Date
brief: The Meridian Digital mobile app version 3.0 is due to launch tomorrow at 9 a.m., announced publicly by the customer. Test sign-off is not complete: 3 high-severity defects are open. The delivery manager proposes deploying tonight and "testing in production". You have 12 visit points to gather what you need and make a decision you can justify.

actions.label: Test lead: impact of the open defects
General condition of the area
actions.note: Nothing of note for the purpose of this visit.

actions.label: Who can approve release with open defects
A staff member: anything else to mention
actions.note: The staff member has nothing further to add on this topic.

actions.label: What the customer has been told
Older records for this area
actions.note: The older records show nothing relevant to this visit.

actions.label: Notices and signs in the area
actions.note: The notices are current and not relevant to this visit.

evidence.text: Open defects: 3 high severity, including DEF-311 where a payment confirmation can be shown twice. Release status in the tool is "approved".
evidence.whyItMatters: Release before planned verification is complete needs an authorized decision; the status contradicts the open defects.
evidence.missedExplanation: Compare the release status with open defects.

evidence.text: Test lead: "DEF-311 affects about 1 percent of payments. The other two are in the new loyalty screen, which can be switched off."
evidence.whyItMatters: The test lead gives clear, factual impact information.
evidence.missedExplanation: Conforming evidence: the facts needed for a decision.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Clear impact facts support a sound decision.

evidence.text: Delivery manager: "The launch is public. We fix forward. Test sign-off is a formality at this point." (note 1)
evidence.whyItMatters: Leadership must support the quality system, including release controls. Calling verification a formality undermines it.
evidence.missedExplanation: Listen for pressure that dismisses controls.

evidence.text: Delivery manager: "Release with open high defects needs the product director, who is reachable tonight."
evidence.falseFindingNote: The defined authority is available. Conforming.

evidence.text: Release procedure RP-1 requires test sign-off or a documented risk acceptance by the product director, and customer agreement where the contract requires it.
Customer contract schedule 3 requires the customer's written acceptance of any release with open high-severity defects. None requested.
evidence.whyItMatters: Customer requirements on release acceptance must be met.
evidence.missedExplanation: Read the contract for acceptance terms.

evidence.text: The loyalty screen sits behind feature flag FF-22, which can be turned off at launch. Turning it off removes 2 of the 3 defects from use.
evidence.whyItMatters: A control is available that reduces risk. Using it is an option for the decision.
evidence.missedExplanation: Look for technical controls that change the options.

evidence.text: Rollback to version 2.9 was rehearsed last week and took 12 minutes.
evidence.falseFindingNote: A rehearsed rollback is good practice.

evidence.text: Customer liaison: "They know testing is tight but do not know about defect DEF-311."
evidence.whyItMatters: Open communication with the customer about known risks supports their decision.

evidence.text: A countdown clock to launch hangs on the wall.
evidence.whyItMatters: A countdown is motivation, not a nonconformity.
evidence.falseFindingNote: The clock is context, not a breach.

evidence.text: The team has ordered food for a late session.
evidence.whyItMatters: Late working is a workload matter to watch, not a quality finding here.
evidence.falseFindingNote: Food orders do not affect conformity.

options: Deploy everything and fix in production
Escalate to the product director now; propose launching with FF-22 off, holding the release until DEF-311 is fixed or the customer accepts it in writing, and keep the rollback ready
Cancel the launch with no explanation
Stay silent; it is not your release
decisions.rationale: This uses the defined authority and the contract, reduces risk with the feature flag, and gives the customer a real choice. Speaking up is part of the role.
optionFeedback: This bypasses release control and the customer's acceptance right.
Proportionate, uses the system, and keeps a launch possible.
Cancelling without explanation ignores options that reduce risk.
Silence leaves a known risk unaddressed.

decisions.prompt: How do you respond to "test sign-off is a formality"?
options: Acknowledge the pressure, restate that sign-off or documented risk acceptance protects the customer and the team, and offer the quickest compliant route
Report the delivery manager to human resources
decisions.rationale: A calm, factual response that offers a route forward addresses both the pressure and the requirement.

containment: Set the release status back to pending until risk acceptance or sign-off
correction: Fix or obtain written customer acceptance for DEF-311 before release
cause: The release tool allows "approved" status with open high-severity defects, and launch dates are announced before test completion
corrective: Block approval in the tool while high defects are open without risk acceptance; set launch dates after a test readiness review
effectiveness: Review the next five releases for status, open defects, and acceptance records

debriefText.found: You found a route that protects the customer and keeps the launch possible.
debriefText.missed: Under pressure, check authority, the contract, and the technical options before deciding.
debriefText.falseFinding: A countdown clock and a food order are not findings.
